title: Dentsply Sirona Supports Ultrasonic Instrumentation Education at Fresno City College
html:
The October 3 event combined hands-on learning and student research presentations, extending a collaboration that began with faculty training into the local dental community.

More than 90 attendees, including dental hygiene students and local dental professionals, gathered at Fresno City College’s Dental Hygiene Clinic on October 3 for an Ultrasonic Instrumentation Day hosted by the college and featuring clinical education from Dentsply Sirona. Titled “Power Moves: Creating Your Ultrasonic Advantage,” the event brought future and practicing clinicians together for a lecture, hands-on learning, and student research presentations—connecting classroom education with the professional community students are preparing to join.

Connecting Classroom Learning With Clinical Practice

At the college’s invitation, Michele Lash, a registered dental hygienist with more than 25 years of experience and Senior Manager, Clinical Research, Perio & Preventive at Dentsply Sirona, led the lecture and hands-on learning.

“One of the most rewarding aspects of clinical education is seeing knowledge shared and multiplied,” said Michele Lash. “Watching Joanne Pacheco and Fred Thomas turn their USTI experience into curriculum enhancements highlights how education can create lasting impact.”

“Our first-year students worked hard on their research posters, and having faculty and professionals in the room gave them a chance to connect with the people they will potentially be working alongside,” said Fred Thomas, Clinic Lead at Fresno City College. “We’re excited to build on and develop educational resources for our community in collaboration with Dentsply Sirona.”

Building on a Collaboration That Began With Faculty Training

The October event grew out of a collaboration that began in November 2024, when Thomas and Joanne Pacheco, Second Year Clinic Coordinator at Fresno City College, attended Dentsply Sirona’s Ultrasonic Scaling Teaching Institute (USTI). Following the training, they revised the program’s first- and second-year curricula, and the college invested in new Cavitron® 300 series scaling systems.

“USTI changed how we think about teaching ultrasonic instrumentation, and we decided to act on it when we got home,” said Joanne Pacheco, Program Director at Fresno City College. “We’re proud that we were able to work with Dentsply Sirona to move quickly, and it is already making a difference in how our students learn.”

In July, Pacheco and Thomas shared their experience with 2026 USTI participants during a virtual panel discussion, describing how the program inspired their curriculum changes and improved student learning.

Supporting Education Across the Profession

Since 2008, USTI has provided faculty with training, clinical experience, and educational resources to teach ultrasonic instrumentation, reaching more than 700 dental hygiene and dental faculty members and impacting more than 51,000 students. The Fresno collaboration connects faculty development with curriculum changes and opportunities for students and practicing professionals to learn together.

“As research, technology, and clinical protocols continue to evolve, it is essential that faculty have access to the latest evidence and educational resources,” said Giorgio Cremaschi, Vice President, Essential Dental Solutions at Dentsply Sirona. “Keeping curricula current helps ensure that students enter the profession prepared to deliver the highest standard of care from day one. Programs like USTI support educators in bringing advances in preventive dental care into the classroom, helping strengthen the future of the profession and ultimately improving patient outcomes.”

About Dentsply Sirona

Dentsply Sirona develops, manufactures, and markets a comprehensive solutions offering, including dental and oral health products as well as other consumable medical devices under a strong portfolio of world-class brands.
